verdict.rationale: A runtime probe records the PlayCanvas engine runtime as MIT-licensed, and the GitHub README calls it an open-source game engine. Together these establish a permissive license for the engine. However, no first-party evidence explicitly states that shipped games owe no royalties, revenue share or per-install fees, and the Editor tooling sits behind paid plans for private projects. missing for 10: explicit first-party statement of no royalties or per-install/runtime fees, documentation of commercial-use terms covering Editor-built projects, independent corroboration of the licensing terms.

support.subject: As a studio lead, the license is permissive with no royalties or per-install fees — I keep what my game earns

citations.quote: PlayCanvas is an open-source game engine built on WebGL2 and WebGPU.
